advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Fix the orphaned indented paragraph in src/rebar/llm/config.py module docstring left by removing the REBAR_LLM_MODEL entry.
evidence: src/rebar/llm/config.py:10: `                          The runner is the provider-agnostic pydantic_ai runtime`
Diff removed the `REBAR_LLM_MODEL DEPRECATED ...` block but retained its continuation lines (the runner description), which were part of that entry.

The new removal test `test_no_prose_doc_advertises_the_variable_as_live` (tests/unit/test_llm_model_env_removal.py:123-133) does NOT include `src/rebar/llm/config.py`, so this orphan is not caught by CI.
advisory.finding: The `src/rebar/llm/config.py` module docstring's 'Environment variables' section now begins with an orphaned, indented paragraph ('The runner is the provider-agnostic pydantic_ai runtime ...') with no leading variable name — leftover from the deleted REBAR_LLM_MODEL entry. It reads as dangling text under the header and mis-attributes the runner description to a nonexistent variable.
advisory.suggested_fix: Re-attach the runner description to its own line (e.g. move it under REBAR_LLM_RUNNER context or drop the indentation) so no dangling text sits under 'Environment variables'.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Update resolve_model docstring line to drop the stale 'env' reference ('config/default').
evidence: src/rebar/llm/config.py:283: `    workflow-level ``model:``, then whatever the config/env/default resolved to.`
Diff updated line 281 to `(``[tool.rebar.llm].model``, else ``DEFAULT_MODEL``)` dropping the env fold, but line 283 still names 'config/env/default'.
advisory.finding: `resolve_model`'s docstring still refers to the env channel ('then whatever the config/env/default resolved to') after the REBAR_LLM_MODEL env rung was removed; the same docstring's precedence line was updated to drop 'env' (now 'step > workflow > config > default'), so the two lines contradict each other.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make test_no_prose_doc_advertises_the_variable_as_live assert on the collected `offenders` (e.g. `assert offenders == []` after a paragraph-scoped removal-context check), not merely file-wide presence of 'removed'.
evidence:
for rel_line in offenders:
        rel = rel_line.split(":", 1)[0]
        text = (root / rel).read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        assert re.search(r"remov|tombston", text, re.I)

The per-line detection collects `offenders.append(...)` but the loop that follows re-reads the whole `text` and asserts a file-wide keyword match, so an actual offending line never fails the test if the file mentions removal anywhere.
Regression-blindness (criterion d): the specific behavior — no live-knob advertisement of REBAR_LLM_MODEL — is not what the assertion verifies.
advisory.finding: The doc guard test_no_prose_doc_advertises_the_variable_as_live cannot detect the regression it names: it builds an `offenders` list of lines that mention REBAR_LLM_MODEL without an inline removal keyword, but the only assertion checks whether the ENTIRE file contains 'remov'/'tombston' anywhere. Since this change adds 'removed' prose to every listed doc, a genuinely regressed line re-advertising the var as a live knob would still pass as long as the word 'removed' appears elsewhere in the file.
advisory.suggested_fix: Scope the removal-context check to the paragraph/neighbouring lines of each offending mention and assert the resulting offender list is empty, so a live-knob line fails even when 'removed' appears elsewhere in the file.
